title: Devon Rice hits the field for the 'Bows, three years after originally committing - NewsBreak
text:
By Rob DeMello ,
1 days ago
Week 3 of Hawaiʻi football spring training camp opened Tuesday, marking the midpoint of the Rainbow Warriors’ preseason work as the team completed its seventh practice.
The running backs room, overseen by offensive coordinator and running backs coach Anthony Arceneaux, returns explosive playmaker Cam Barfield along with several other capable options. In Hawaiʻi’s run-and-shoot offense, the position traditionally emphasizes versatility, with an added premium on pass protection and receiving ability out of the backfield.
One player aiming to add depth is Kansas State transfer Devon Rice. The Bishop Gorman product originally committed to Hawaiʻi in 2023 and said his path back to Manoa felt inevitable after a winding journey.
Rice said his decision was influenced by long-standing relationships with the coaching staff, including Chris Brown, and connections with several current players. He also pointed to his close relationship with quarterback Micah Alejado as another factor in his return to the islands.
“I’m a firm believer that God works in mysterious ways,” Rice said. “No matter the journey, I’m here at this moment, and I just want to do my part and help this team.”
Rice added that he is willing to fill any role needed, to put the team in the best position to win.
“Whether that’s being in the slot, blocking all day, running the ball no matter what. Even if I got to throw the ball, I mean, whatever you want me to do, I’m, gonna do it.,” said Rice. “As long as that puts the team in the best position to win.”
The Rainbow Warriors currently have six running backs on the spring roster as camp continues through March 6.
